title: Qwen completion attempts — superseded
description: Completion diagnostics before switching the OCR stage to PaddleOCR-VL-1.6.
body:
## Setup notes before this baseline

One GPU was too slow for practical iteration, so we moved to four L4 GPUs. We kept the three smallest PDFs and one warm-up plus one timed call per PDF.

The initial 2,048-token cap truncated pages 1 and 3 of the seaplane report. Repeated calls matched the same incomplete references, so their reference-fidelity checks passed. That run was rejected as a baseline. [Setup notes](#/doc/experiments/000-setup-notes).

## What must work first

Every page must finish generation with EOS. The output allowance is now **8,192 tokens per page**; reaching an allowance without EOS raises an error and prevents reference capture. A complete transcription normally stops earlier.

Page 1 also repeated figure captions. The prompt now explicitly requests each text element once, all table rows, original language and column order, and visible plot labels without invented plot data. This is a baseline correctness repair; it establishes new reference outputs.

Reference capture saves individual page transcriptions for inspection against all seven PDF pages. EOS verifies normal termination, while the page review checks coverage of text, headings and tables. This is not a formal character-level OCR accuracy benchmark.

## Controlled setup

The same four L4 GPUs, one full Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct replica per GPU, one page per GPU call, bf16, SDPA, greedy decoding and 150 DPI. The clarified prompt and output allowance are fixed for this baseline and subsequent optimizations. Pages are reassembled in original order. Chunking targets 512 tokens; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B runs in fp32 on GPU 0.

The selected PDFs remain the two complete earthquake checklists and complete three-page seaplane report. The larger library has ten PDFs, each at most five pages. PDF bytes remain unchanged.

## Evaluation

After reviewing reference capture, evaluate each PDF sequentially with **one warm-up and one timed call**. Every call must match the complete reference's OCR bytes, chunk count/order/IDs/dimensions, and embeddings at cosine ≥ 0.99. Startup and reference capture are excluded from timed latency. One timed sample per PDF is not an official speedup comparison.

Inspect per-PDF latency first; pooled percentiles describe this small heterogeneous selection rather than repeat variability.

## Current status

Stopped at the user's request. An exact 8,192-token rerun saved repeated paragraphs on NACA page 2 and rejected the unfinished generation. Penalties 1.05 and 1.1 also failed to finish page 1 in separate bounded diagnostics.

The active baseline has switched to [PaddleOCR-VL-1.6](#/doc/experiments/004-paddleocr-baseline). No Qwen reference from these attempts was accepted.
